rv.q: So a dreamy production in its look and sound but you do not feel like you have quite entered into its enchantments.
It’s just a bit disjointed, and less of a laugh than it should be.

Music trained, all are terrific. Oberon and Titania (Olivier Huband and Jenny Rainsford—also Theseus and Hippolyta) sing, too, entitled rock stars. Many celebrities in the audience respond more than others I notice—they get it.

Funny but unmagical A Midsummer Night’s Dream Atri Al Ghussain Jenny Rainford London Mary Malone Nadeem Islam Naomi Dawson Olivier Huband Regent’s Air Theatre Review Theatre Tomás Palmer William Shakespeare
This A Midsummer Night’s Dream is an enjoyable if uneven affair.
It is an inventive, inclusive and hugely entertaining production that reminds us why Shakespeare's most magical comedy continues to cast its spell.
Atri Banerjee's 2026 punt gives the play a folk-rock aesthetic, complete with a punkish fairy band and neon dip dyed hair Titania, but ultimately struggles to take flight.
Whilst some choices feel somewhat clunky within the motion of the play, others are revelations that invigorate the work.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this folk-infused production, with praise for Memon's music and moments of humor, but many find Banerjee's vision lacks coherence and fails to utilize the outdoor setting effectively.

ru.inst: £5 standing tickets released Fridays @ 11 AM via Globe's website.
